questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “This is the first time I ____ such an interpretation.”
questions.why: 'This is the first time' takes the present perfect. GPSC CBRT, Jan 2026.

questions.q: Identify the clause type: “Whatever he says does not matter.”
questions.why: The clause is the subject of 'does not matter', so it is a noun clause. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The nurse is dressing the wound.”
opts: The wound is being dressed by the nurse.
The wound was being dressed by the nurse.
The wound is been dressed by the nurse.
The wound is dressed by the nurse.
questions.why: Present continuous passive: is being + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct transformation of: “He is too proud to apologise.”
opts: He is very proud and he apologises.
He is proud enough to apologise.
He is so proud that he will not apologise.
He is so proud that he will apologise.
questions.why: too … to = so … that … not. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.
Double c, double r, -ence. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the clause type: “I know that he is innocent.”
questions.why: 'That he is innocent' is the object of 'know'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The clerk ordered pens, files and other office ____.”
questions.why: 'Stationery' means writing materials; 'stationary' means not moving. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: “She hardly ever complains, ____?”
questions.why: 'Hardly' is negative, so the tag is positive. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The clerk has not filed the application.”
opts: The application was not filed by the clerk.
The application has not been filed by the clerk.
The application is not being filed by the clerk.
The application has not filed by the clerk.
questions.why: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: “I would rather ____ at home than go out in this rain.”
questions.why: 'Would rather' takes the bare infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.
